interest: Limiting Japanese naval visits in Hawaii and the Hayatomo telephone incident.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.3311A) covers U.S. policy and incidents concerning visits of Japanese public and naval vessels to ports in the Hawaiian Islands between November 1937 and June 1938 (along with an earlier 1931 administrative clearance note). The file begins with a November 1937 interdepartmental recommendation to the President that permission for Japanese public vessels be restricted to the port of Honolulu to prevent access to outlying Hawaiian ports. The primary episode documented in the file took place in May 1938, when Brian Bedford, an American repairman for the Mutual Telephone Company, was obstructed, detained, and searched by armed guards and Japanese sailors aboard the naval tanker Hayatomo docked at U.S. Naval Pier 5-A in Honolulu while attempting to retrieve a company telephone. The correspondence documents the telephone company's formal protest and ultimatum sent to Japanese Consul-General Kosaku Midzusawa, the transmission of the report through 14th Naval District Commandant Admiral Orin G. Murfin and Acting Secretary of the Navy William D. Leahy to the State Department, and the State Department's internal determination that the matter required no official diplomatic action.
